title: Up and Over
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 3169, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 3169 · constellation Sextans · about 70 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Hubble catches the spiral galaxy NGC 3169 from a steep angle, so the viewer seems to be stretching up to peer over a wall toward the galaxy's bright center. That wall is the thick dust woven through the galaxy's spiral arms.

Spiral galaxies are common sights, and what makes this one worth a second look is the viewpoint. Dust in space is a mixture of many kinds of particles, among them water ice, hydrocarbons and silicates, along with other solid material. It comes from many places. Some is left over from the birth of stars and planets, and some consists of molecules that starlight has altered over millions of years.

NGC 3169 lies about 70 million light-years away in the constellation Sextans (The Sextant). It belongs to the Leo I Group of galaxies. Like the Local Group that contains our Milky Way, the Leo I Group is one part of a much larger gathering called the Virgo Supercluster.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.29 x 2.10 arcminutes) and distance (70 million light years), the frame spans roughly 67,000 × 43,000 light-years. Its light set out about 70 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys observed NGC 3169 in visible red and near-infrared light. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: One of the filters records near-infrared light, which the eye cannot see, and a galaxy this far away is far too faint for unaided eyes.

behind.people: See full credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, L. Ho
behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The picture was released as an ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week. It was made with Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys through two filters, one tuned to a wavelength of 658 nanometers and one to 814 nanometers in the near-infrared.
alt: A spiral galaxy seen at a sharp angle, its bright center partly hidden behind thick dust in its spiral arms.
